findings.text: The node's brief named this fragment as a write path and instructed it to write its landing record and evidence anchor here, but the file is not produced: it does not exist at the reviewed head 1c2a3b943 and is absent from the node's changed_paths. The landing evidence (the 12-to-0 gate, the two test arms and the per-driver figure-path map) lives only in the out-of-repo report .config/reckon/crew/reports/nova/s22/fsa-wall-mask-solovev-and-sol.md, so the repo carries no evidence anchor for this node's claim.

Routing the overlay panel's two series through draw_scattered_contours, which hard-codes linestyles="solid" (nova/media/poloidal.py:268), removes the dashed cue that distinguished the control field (linewidth 0.9) from the SOL field (1.25) - both are drawn from the same viridis colour list - so the overlay now separates them by width alone. solovev_cut_cell_moments' image series likewise loses its dash, though there colour still separates it from the exact field. The node discloses this as a follow-on; restoring the cue needs an optional linestyles parameter on the painter.

Both arms independently reproduced by this review at the reviewed worktrees: head 1c2a3b943 -> 35 passed in 119.78s EXIT=0 (logs/review-tests-head.log), base 68762d363 -> 35 passed in 104.44s EXIT=0 (logs/review-tests-base.log). The node's declared negative control (the scanner's base arm) was reproduced byte-for-byte: 12 unguarded sites, EXIT=1.

justifications.durability: The rule is enforced where it cannot silently regress: draw_scattered_contours makes wall a required positional parameter and masks every triangle that leaves the vessel, and draw_flux_contours blanks grid points outside the wall units it is given, so a routed call carries the mask by construction rather than by a comment. The read-only scanner gate locks the batch and now reports 0 where base reported 12, and I confirmed it fires when a site is unmasked. Weaknesses. The scanner is wired to nothing but a manual pytest/manual CLI run - no conftest, pyproject or CI reference imports it - so only a later reader runs it. The disclosed legibility loss is untested: draw_scattered_contours hard-codes linestyles="solid" (nova/media/poloidal.py:268), so in sol_current_demonstration's overlay panel the control (linewidth 0.9) and SOL (1.25) series now share one colour list and differ by width alone, and in solovev_cut_cell_moments the dashed image series becomes solid at the same 0.42 width as the exact field (colour still separates them). The node reports this honestly as a follow-on but adds no test pinning the intended cue.
justifications.evidence: The record is strong where it counts: a real, reproduced negative control, both test arms logged, and a read-only gate that both fires and clears. I reproduced the scanner's base arm (12 sites, EXIT=1, logs/review-tests-base-scan-equivalent) and head arm (0 sites, EXIT=0) exactly; reproduced both focused-test arms (35 passed each); and added an independent falsification the node did not run - reverting the wall-masked call in a scratch copy of the head benchmarks/solovev_off_axis_census.py to a bare axis.tricontour makes the scanner report the scratch file's line 431 tricontour and exit 1, so the green head arm is a real clear and not a scanner that never fires. Deductions: the node's granted evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/figure-and-solver-audit/fsa-wall-mask-solovev-and-sol.html, which the brief named as the place to write the landing record and evidence anchor, was not produced - it does not exist at the reviewed head, is absent from the node's changed_paths, and the landing evidence lives only in the out-of-repo report under .config/reckon/crew/reports/, so no in-repo anchor records the claim; and there is no render-level proof the mask clips the field at the vessel, only the static routing, so the drawing effect itself is unverified (the brief forbade re-rendering here, so this is a scope-of-evidence limit rather than a defect).
justifications.fit: Minimal and idiomatic: the change reuses the two committed wall-masked painters rather than adding machinery: no new module, dependency or abstraction, and no plan/sprint/ticket identifier in names, comments or the commit. The added Carrier.wall field and the wall_rz_m entry in plot_data are the natural way to carry the wall the driver already holds to the painter, and the certificate change is a one-keyword addition at each of three sites. Deductions: the same wall-mask tension across two figure families (blanked raster for grid-drawn fields, masked triangulation for scattered-node fields) is now spread across five drivers with no shared helper, so a sixth driver must rediscover which painter its data needs; and the lost-dash cue is a small expressiveness regression the painter could have avoided.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The reviewed run's goal - route every unguarded scattered-field contour call in the batch through a wall-masked painter so no figure draws field outside the vessel - is met and independently reproduced. The scanner tests/renderer_wall_scan.py at the reviewed head 1c2a3b943 reports nothing and exits 0; at base 68762d363 it reports exactly the 12 sites the brief named (solovev_certificate 1967/2045/2048 draw_flux_contours; solovev_solver_discriminator 542/550 tricontour; solovev_off_axis_census 427 tricontour; solovev_cut_cell_moments 804/812/820 tricontour; sol_current_demonstration 494/527/535 tricontour) and exits 1 - both reproduced first-hand and matching the node's logs. The two draw_flux_contours sites in the certificate _plot and the one in _draw_error_contours now pass wall=, and every direct tricontour moves to draw_scattered_contours, whose wall argument is required and whose triangles are masked against the vessel. The report's per-driver figure paths were verified against the drivers: gs-absolute-accuracy/solovev/{case}-production-route-{cells}.png (solovev_certificate.py:267), uniform-cell-clip-and-coupling/solver-discriminator/error-maps.svg and exact-axis-control-error-maps.svg (:53-54), off-axis-error/error-contours.svg beside census.json (:38-41), cut-cell-moments/error-maps.svg (:50), sol-current-demonstration/{flux-map-contours,current-profiles}.svg (:808-809) - all correct. Not full marks only because no figure was re-rendered, so the routing is verified statically rather than by a rendered panel (by design, per the brief).
justifications.scope_discipline: The single reviewed commit 1c2a3b943 touches exactly five files - benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py, benchmarks/solovev_solver_discriminator.py, benchmarks/solovev_off_axis_census.py, benchmarks/solovev_cut_cell_moments.py, benchmarks/sol_current_demonstration.py - all inside the node's granted write paths, and no source under nova/ is edited, exactly as the brief required. The commit subject is conventional and the body explains each driver's route and the line-style follow-on; there is no Co-Authored-By or other AI trailer and no bodiless message. A scan of the added diff lines for banned plan/stage/ticket labels returns only matplotlib colour names (color="C3"), which are not violations. Deducted for one declared-scope deliverable left unwritten: the granted write path docs/evidence/fragments/figure-and-solver-audit/fsa-wall-mask-solovev-and-sol.html was in the node's own orientation_write_paths and the brief required the landing record there, but it is not produced.

SCORE goal_fidelity: 19
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: The reviewed run's goal - route every unguarded scattered-field contour call in the batch through a wall-masked painter so no figure draws field outside the vessel - is met and independently reproduced. The scanner reports nothing at the reviewed head and exactly the 12 brief-named sites at base (EXIT 0 -> 1), both reproduced first-hand. Every tricontour moves to draw_scattered_contours (wall required, triangles masked) and the three certificate draw_flux_contours calls pass wall=. The report's per-driver figure paths verified against the drivers (all correct). No figure was re-rendered (by design), so verification is static.
SCORE evidence: 16
JUSTIFICATION evidence: Reproduced the scanner base arm (12 sites, EXIT=1) and head arm (0 sites, EXIT=0), both focused-test arms (35 passed each), and added an independent falsification: unmasking one head site in a scratch copy makes the scanner fire (scratch line 431 tricontour, EXIT=1), so the green head arm is a real clear and not a scanner that never fires. Deductions: the granted in-repo evidence fragment was not produced (landing evidence lives only in the out-of-repo report), and there is no render-level proof the mask clips the field at the vessel.
SCORE scope_discipline: 18
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: The one reviewed commit touches exactly the five granted benchmark files, no nova/ source, subject conventional with a real body, no AI trailer, and added lines carry no banned labels (only matplotlib colour names). Deducted for the granted fragment write path left unwritten.
SCORE durability: 16
JUSTIFICATION durability: Mask enforced by construction in both painters; the read-only scanner locks the batch at 0 and demonstrably fires when a site is unmasked. Weaknesses: the scanner is wired to nothing but a manual run (no conftest/CI), and the disclosed line-style regression is not pinned by a test.
SCORE fit: 18
JUSTIFICATION fit: Minimal and idiomatic - reuses the two committed painters, no new module/dependency/abstraction, no plan label. Deductions: the raster-vs-scattered painter choice is re-derived in each of five drivers, and the lost dash cue is a small expressiveness regression.
